title: Subset preservation conjecture for multiple monotone submodular functions
statement:
Let $l\geq 1$ be a constant, let $f_1,\dots,f_l$ be monotone submodular functions on a ground set $N$, and let $S\subseteq N$ have size $k$ with $f_i(S)\geq V_i$ for every $i\in[l]$. For an integer $m$ satisfying $s\geq m\geq l$, there should exist a set $X\subseteq S$ of size $m$ such that

$$
f_i(X)\geq \frac{m-\Theta(1)}{k}V_i,\quad \forall i\in[l].
$$

**Subset preservation conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, such a set $X$ exists. The claim would provide a simultaneous value guarantee for a constant number of monotone submodular objectives when reducing the cardinality of a feasible set; whether this general statement holds remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.06616

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).
source_name: James B. Orlin, Andreas S. Schulz and Rajan Udwani, “Robust Monotone Submodular Function Maximization”, arXiv:1507.06616 (2017).
